# Story 1.2: Tableau Extension Shell & Initialization Status: ready-for-dev ## Story As an **admin**, I want the autom9 extension to load inside a Tableau dashboard without errors, so that consultants see the extension panel and the system is ready to make backend calls. ## Acceptance Criteria 1. **Given** the `.trex` manifest is registered in Tableau Desktop or Tableau Cloud **When** a consultant opens a Tableau dashboard with the autom9 extension **Then** the extension panel renders without a blank screen or error message 2. **Given** the extension panel has mounted **When** `tableau.extensions.initializeAsync()` is called **Then** no store initialization or backend HTTP calls begin until the promise resolves **And** if `initializeAsync()` rejects, the extension displays a clear load-failure message 3. **Given** the extension is running in development **When** the extension frontend makes an HTTP call to the backend **Then** CORS headers are accepted for the configured Tableau origins (no CORS errors in browser console) 4. **Given** any Tableau Dashboard (Desktop or Cloud/Server) **When** the extension is loaded **Then** the extension shell renders correctly in both environments (FR29) ## Tasks / Subtasks - [ ] **Task 1: Add Tableau Extensions API runtime script to `index.html`** (AC: 1, 2, 4) - [ ] Add script tag before closing `` in `autom9-extension/index.html`: ```html ``` - [ ] This is the runtime that provides `window.tableau` — without it `initializeAsync` is undefined even with the types package installed - [ ] **Task 2: Create `autom9.trex` manifest** (AC: 1, 4) - [ ] Create `autom9-extension/autom9.trex` with exact XML structure below (Tableau ignores non-XML content): ```xml en_US 1.4 http://localhost:5173 read autom9 AI planning assistant for consultants ``` - [ ] `source-location` URL = the extension frontend URL (Vite dev server at localhost:5173). This is NOT the backend URL. The backend URL is configured separately via `VITE_BACKEND_URL`. - [ ] `id` must be unique reverse-DNS format; `min-api-version` 1.4 supports Tableau Desktop 2019.4+ - [ ] `permission` value `read` = read worksheet data; do NOT add write permissions - [ ] **Task 3: Add `CORS_ORIGINS` to backend config and wire CORS middleware** (AC: 3) - [ ] In `autom9-backend/app/core/config.py`, add one field to `Settings` class: ```python CORS_ORIGINS: str = "http://localhost:5173" ``` Use a default so existing tests are unaffected. Comma-separated list format: `"http://localhost:5173,https://prod.tableau.com"`. - [ ] In `autom9-backend/app/main.py`, add CORS middleware **before** route definitions (order matters in ASGI middleware stack): ```python from fastapi.middleware.cors import CORSMiddleware app.add_middleware( CORSMiddleware, allow_origins=[o.strip() for o in settings.CORS_ORIGINS.split(",")], allow_credentials=True, allow_methods=["*"], allow_headers=["*"], ) ``` - [ ] Update `autom9-backend/.env.example`: add `CORS_ORIGINS=http://localhost:5173` - [ ] Update root `docker-compose.yml` `app` service `environment:` block: add `CORS_ORIGINS: ${CORS_ORIGINS:-http://localhost:5173}` - [ ] **Task 4: Create `src/lib/tableau.ts` — Tableau API wrapper** (AC: 2) - [ ] Create `autom9-extension/src/lib/tableau.ts`: ```typescript /** * Thin wrapper around window.tableau.extensions.initializeAsync(). * Resolves immediately when Tableau runtime is absent (dev/test environment). */ export async function initializeExtension(): Promise { if (typeof window === 'undefined' || !('tableau' in window)) { // No Tableau runtime — running in dev/test outside Tableau Desktop/Cloud return; } await (window as typeof window & { tableau: { extensions: { initializeAsync: () => Promise } } }) .tableau.extensions.initializeAsync(); } ``` - [ ] Do NOT use `import tableau from '@tableau/extensions-api-types'` — the types package provides ambient type declarations only; the runtime is the CDN script. Access via `window.tableau` cast. - [ ] Do NOT call `initializeAsync()` more than once — Tableau throws if called on an already-initialized extension. - [ ] **Task 5: Create `src/lib/api.ts` — backend HTTP client scaffold** (architecture requirement; used fully in Story 1.3) - [ ] Create `autom9-extension/src/lib/api.ts`: ```typescript const BACKEND_URL = import.meta.env.VITE_BACKEND_URL ?? 'http://localhost:8000'; export class ApiError extends Error { constructor( public readonly code: string, message: string, public readonly status: number, ) { super(message); this.name = 'ApiError'; } } export async function apiFetch( path: string, init?: RequestInit, ): Promise { let response: Response; try { response = await fetch(`${BACKEND_URL}${path}`, { ...init, headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json', ...init?.headers, }, }); } catch (err) { throw new ApiError('NETWORK_ERROR', 'Unable to reach the autom9 backend', 0); } if (!response.ok) { let code = 'UNKNOWN_ERROR'; let message = `Request failed with status ${response.status}`; try { const body = await response.json(); code = body?.error?.code ?? code; message = body?.error?.message ?? message; } catch { // non-JSON error body — keep defaults } throw new ApiError(code, message, response.status); } return response.json() as Promise; } ``` - [ ] JSON field names from the API are `snake_case`; camelCase conversion for internal Svelte state is done at the call site, NOT inside `apiFetch`. See architecture API envelope spec. - [ ] `VITE_BACKEND_URL` is a Vite env var (must be prefixed `VITE_` to be exposed to client bundle). - [ ] Create `autom9-extension/.env.example` with: `VITE_BACKEND_URL=http://localhost:8000` - [ ] **Task 6: Replace `App.svelte` with initialization gate** (AC: 1, 2) - [ ] Replace the entire contents of `autom9-extension/src/App.svelte` with: ```svelte {#if status === 'loading'}

Loading autom9…

{:else if status === 'error'}

autom9 failed to load

{errorMessage}

{:else}

autom9 ready.

{/if} ``` - [ ] `$state` is a Svelte 5 rune — valid inside `.svelte` files without `.svelte.ts` extension - [ ] No stores are initialized here; no backend HTTP calls are made here — the gate enforces this (AC2) - [ ] Delete `autom9-extension/src/lib/Counter.svelte` — dead default scaffold code - [ ] **Task 7: Write backend CORS tests** (AC: 3) - [ ] Add `autom9-backend/tests/test_cors.py`: ```python import pytest from httpx import AsyncClient, ASGITransport from app.main import app @pytest.mark.asyncio async def test_cors_allowed_origin_returns_header(): async with AsyncClient( transport=ASGITransport(app=app), base_url="http://test" ) as client: response = await client.get( "/health", headers={"Origin": "http://localhost:5173"}, ) assert response.status_code == 200 assert response.headers.get("access-control-allow-origin") == "http://localhost:5173" @pytest.mark.asyncio async def test_cors_preflight_allowed_origin(): async with AsyncClient( transport=ASGITransport(app=app), base_url="http://test" ) as client: response = await client.options( "/health", headers={ "Origin": "http://localhost:5173", "Access-Control-Request-Method": "POST", "Access-Control-Request-Headers": "Content-Type", }, ) assert response.status_code == 200 assert "access-control-allow-origin" in response.headers @pytest.mark.asyncio async def test_cors_disallowed_origin_no_acao_header(): async with AsyncClient( transport=ASGITransport(app=app), base_url="http://test" ) as client: response = await client.get( "/health", headers={"Origin": "http://evil.example.com"}, ) assert response.status_code == 200 assert response.headers.get("access-control-allow-origin") != "http://evil.example.com" ``` - [ ] These tests use the real `app` instance with the real `Settings()` — ensure test environment has required env vars set (existing conftest handles this via `monkeypatch` / module-level env setup) - [ ] ⚠️ If `Settings()` fails at import time during tests, check that `conftest.py` sets all required env vars before `app.main` is imported. The CORS test file imports `app.main` directly. - [ ] **Task 8: Verify frontend build** (AC: 1, 4) - [ ] Run `npm run build` from `autom9-extension/` — must produce `dist/` with no errors - [ ] Run `npm run check` from `autom9-extension/` — svelte-check + tsc must pass with no type errors - [ ] Fix any TypeScript errors introduced by the new files before marking this task complete ## Dev Notes ### Architecture Source All decisions for this story: `_bmad-output/planning-artifacts/architecture.md` — "Frontend Architecture", "Gap Analysis Results" (items 1–4), "API & Communication Patterns" (CORS), and "Implementation Handoff". ### Critical: `.trex` `source-location` is the extension frontend URL, not the backend The `.trex` file tells Tableau where to load the extension HTML. In dev this is `http://localhost:5173` (the Vite dev server). In production it would be the hosted extension URL. The backend is at a different port (8000) and is never referenced in `.trex`. ### Critical: Svelte 5 `$state` rune in `.svelte` files `$state` runes are valid inside `

import pytest
import pytest_asyncio
from httpx import ASGITransport, AsyncClient
from sqlalchemy import event
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession, create_async_engine
from sqlalchemy.pool import NullPool

from app.db.base import Base
from app.db.deps import get_db
from app.main import app

TEST_DATABASE_URL = os.environ["DATABASE_URL"]


@pytest_asyncio.fixture(scope="session")
async def engine():
    test_engine = create_async_engine(TEST_DATABASE_URL, poolclass=NullPool)
    async with test_engine.begin() as conn:
        await conn.run_sync(Base.metadata.create_all)
    yield test_engine
    async with test_engine.begin() as conn:
        await conn.run_sync(Base.metadata.drop_all)
    await test_engine.dispose()


@pytest_asyncio.fixture(scope="function")
async def db_session(engine):
    async with engine.connect() as connection:
        await connection.begin()
        await connection.begin_nested()
        session = AsyncSession(connection, expire_on_commit=False)

        @event.listens_for(session.sync_session, "after_transaction_end")
        def restart_savepoint(sess, transaction):
            if transaction.nested and not transaction._parent.nested:
                sess.begin_nested()

        yield session
        await session.close()
        await connection.rollback()


@pytest_asyncio.fixture(scope="function")
async def client(db_session):
    async def override_get_db():
        yield db_session

    app.dependency_overrides[get_db] = override_get_db
    async with AsyncClient(transport=ASGITransport(app=app), base_url="http://test") as ac:
        yield ac
    app.dependency_overrides.pop(get_db, None)

# Story 1.2: Tableau Extension Shell & Initialization Status: ready-for-dev ## Story As an **admin**, I want the autom9 extension to load inside a Tableau dashboard without errors, so that consultants see the extension panel and the system is ready to make backend calls. ## Acceptance Criteria 1. **Given** the `.trex` manifest is registered in Tableau Desktop or Tableau Cloud **When** a consultant opens a Tableau dashboard with the autom9 extension **Then** the extension panel renders without a blank screen or error message 2. **Given** the extension panel has mounted **When** `tableau.extensions.initializeAsync()` is called **Then** no store initialization or backend HTTP calls begin until the promise resolves **And** if `initializeAsync()` rejects, the extension displays a clear load-failure message 3. **Given** the extension is running in development **When** the extension frontend makes an HTTP call to the backend **Then** CORS headers are accepted for the configured Tableau origins (no CORS errors in browser console) 4. **Given** any Tableau Dashboard (Desktop or Cloud/Server) **When** the extension is loaded **Then** the extension shell renders correctly in both environments (FR29) ## Tasks / Subtasks - [ ] **Task 1: Add Tableau Extensions API runtime script to `index.html`** (AC: 1, 2, 4) - [ ] Add script tag before closing `` in `autom9-extension/index.html`: ```html ``` - [ ] This is the runtime that provides `window.tableau` — without it `initializeAsync` is undefined even with the types package installed - [ ] **Task 2: Create `autom9.trex` manifest** (AC: 1, 4) - [ ] Create `autom9-extension/autom9.trex` with exact XML structure below (Tableau ignores non-XML content): ```xml en_US 1.4 http://localhost:5173 read autom9 AI planning assistant for consultants ``` - [ ] `source-location` URL = the extension frontend URL (Vite dev server at localhost:5173). This is NOT the backend URL. The backend URL is configured separately via `VITE_BACKEND_URL`. - [ ] `id` must be unique reverse-DNS format; `min-api-version` 1.4 supports Tableau Desktop 2019.4+ - [ ] `permission` value `read` = read worksheet data; do NOT add write permissions - [ ] **Task 3: Add `CORS_ORIGINS` to backend config and wire CORS middleware** (AC: 3) - [ ] In `autom9-backend/app/core/config.py`, add one field to `Settings` class: ```python CORS_ORIGINS: str = "http://localhost:5173" ``` Use a default so existing tests are unaffected. Comma-separated list format: `"http://localhost:5173,https://prod.tableau.com"`. - [ ] In `autom9-backend/app/main.py`, add CORS middleware **before** route definitions (order matters in ASGI middleware stack): ```python from fastapi.middleware.cors import CORSMiddleware app.add_middleware( CORSMiddleware, allow_origins=[o.strip() for o in settings.CORS_ORIGINS.split(",")], allow_credentials=True, allow_methods=["*"], allow_headers=["*"], ) ``` - [ ] Update `autom9-backend/.env.example`: add `CORS_ORIGINS=http://localhost:5173` - [ ] Update root `docker-compose.yml` `app` service `environment:` block: add `CORS_ORIGINS: ${CORS_ORIGINS:-http://localhost:5173}` - [ ] **Task 4: Create `src/lib/tableau.ts` — Tableau API wrapper** (AC: 2) - [ ] Create `autom9-extension/src/lib/tableau.ts`: ```typescript /** * Thin wrapper around window.tableau.extensions.initializeAsync(). * Resolves immediately when Tableau runtime is absent (dev/test environment). */ export async function initializeExtension(): Promise { if (typeof window === 'undefined' || !('tableau' in window)) { // No Tableau runtime — running in dev/test outside Tableau Desktop/Cloud return; } await (window as typeof window & { tableau: { extensions: { initializeAsync: () => Promise } } }) .tableau.extensions.initializeAsync(); } ``` - [ ] Do NOT use `import tableau from '@tableau/extensions-api-types'` — the types package provides ambient type declarations only; the runtime is the CDN script. Access via `window.tableau` cast. - [ ] Do NOT call `initializeAsync()` more than once — Tableau throws if called on an already-initialized extension. - [ ] **Task 5: Create `src/lib/api.ts` — backend HTTP client scaffold** (architecture requirement; used fully in Story 1.3) - [ ] Create `autom9-extension/src/lib/api.ts`: ```typescript const BACKEND_URL = import.meta.env.VITE_BACKEND_URL ?? 'http://localhost:8000'; export class ApiError extends Error { constructor( public readonly code: string, message: string, public readonly status: number, ) { super(message); this.name = 'ApiError'; } } export async function apiFetch( path: string, init?: RequestInit, ): Promise { let response: Response; try { response = await fetch(`${BACKEND_URL}${path}`, { ...init, headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json', ...init?.headers, }, }); } catch (err) { throw new ApiError('NETWORK_ERROR', 'Unable to reach the autom9 backend', 0); } if (!response.ok) { let code = 'UNKNOWN_ERROR'; let message = `Request failed with status ${response.status}`; try { const body = await response.json(); code = body?.error?.code ?? code; message = body?.error?.message ?? message; } catch { // non-JSON error body — keep defaults } throw new ApiError(code, message, response.status); } return response.json() as Promise; } ``` - [ ] JSON field names from the API are `snake_case`; camelCase conversion for internal Svelte state is done at the call site, NOT inside `apiFetch`. See architecture API envelope spec. - [ ] `VITE_BACKEND_URL` is a Vite env var (must be prefixed `VITE_` to be exposed to client bundle). - [ ] Create `autom9-extension/.env.example` with: `VITE_BACKEND_URL=http://localhost:8000` - [ ] **Task 6: Replace `App.svelte` with initialization gate** (AC: 1, 2) - [ ] Replace the entire contents of `autom9-extension/src/App.svelte` with: ```svelte {#if status === 'loading'}

Loading autom9…

{:else if status === 'error'}

autom9 failed to load

{errorMessage}

{:else}

## Dev Notes

### Architecture Source
All decisions for this story: `_bmad-output/planning-artifacts/architecture.md` — "Frontend Architecture", "Gap Analysis Results" (items 1–4), "API & Communication Patterns" (CORS), and "Implementation Handoff".

### Critical: `.trex` `source-location` is the extension frontend URL, not the backend
The `.trex` file tells Tableau where to load the extension HTML. In dev this is `http://localhost:5173` (the Vite dev server). In production it would be the hosted extension URL. The backend is at a different port (8000) and is never referenced in `.trex`.

### Critical: Svelte 5 `$state` rune in `.svelte` files
`$state` runes are valid inside `<script>` blocks in `.svelte` components without the `.svelte.ts` extension. The `.svelte.ts` extension is required only for standalone TypeScript files that use runes outside a component (e.g., store files in `src/stores/`). `App.svelte` is a component — `$state` works there directly.

### Critical: Do not use `writable()` from `svelte/store`
That is the Svelte 4 API. Svelte 5 uses class-based `$state` in `.svelte.ts` files for stores. No stores are created in this story — stores are Story 1.3+ — but do not import from `svelte/store` anywhere.

### Critical: CORS middleware order in FastAPI
`app.add_middleware()` must be called after `app = FastAPI(...)` but BEFORE `@app.get(...)` route decorators are defined, otherwise preflight OPTIONS requests may not match the middleware. In `app/main.py`, add middleware immediately after `app = FastAPI(title="autom9", lifespan=lifespan)`.

### Critical: `CORS_ORIGINS` field has a default — not breaking
`CORS_ORIGINS: str = "http://localhost:5173"` has a Python default, so it is not a required pydantic-settings field. Existing tests pass `ValidationError` checks without setting it. All six currently required fields remain required.

### Backend settings rename (from Story 1.1 review decision)
The spec originally named these `DATABASE_POOL_MIN` and `DATABASE_POOL_MAX`. The implementation renamed them to `DATABASE_POOL_BASE` and `DATABASE_POOL_OVERFLOW` (accepted in review). Do NOT rename them back. This affects `app/core/config.py`, `app/db/engine.py`, `docker-compose.yml`, `.env.example`, and `tests/conftest.py`.

### CORS test environment isolation
The CORS tests in `test_cors.py` import `app.main` which triggers `Settings()` at module import. The conftest must establish env vars before this import. If tests are run in isolation (`pytest tests/test_cors.py`) and conftest env setup hasn't run, the import fails. Run the full suite (`pytest`) to ensure conftest ordering. This is a known caveat from Story 1.1 (deferred: "Module-level engine + settings creation couples production config to test import chain").

### Tableau Extensions API type access
The `@tableau/extensions-api-types` package (1.16.0 installed) provides ambient TypeScript declarations. Access `tableau` through `window` with an explicit cast — do not `import tableau from ...` as there is no default export. The runtime is the CDN script added to `index.html`.

### `initializeAsync()` in dev without Tableau runtime
When `npm run dev` is run outside Tableau Desktop/Cloud, `window.tableau` is undefined (the CDN script is unreachable or the Tableau object is not injected). The `initializeExtension()` wrapper in `tableau.ts` detects this and resolves immediately, allowing the extension shell to render in `ready` state in a normal browser. This is intentional — it enables development iteration without requiring Tableau Desktop.

# Story 1.2: Tableau Extension Shell & Initialization Status: ready-for-dev ## Story As an **admin**, I want the autom9 extension to load inside a Tableau dashboard without errors, so that consultants see the extension panel and the system is ready to make backend calls. ## Acceptance Criteria 1. **Given** the `.trex` manifest is registered in Tableau Desktop or Tableau Cloud **When** a consultant opens a Tableau dashboard with the autom9 extension **Then** the extension panel renders without a blank screen or error message 2. **Given** the extension panel has mounted **When** `tableau.extensions.initializeAsync()` is called **Then** no store initialization or backend HTTP calls begin until the promise resolves **And** if `initializeAsync()` rejects, the extension displays a clear load-failure message 3. **Given** the extension is running in development **When** the extension frontend makes an HTTP call to the backend **Then** CORS headers are accepted for the configured Tableau origins (no CORS errors in browser console) 4. **Given** any Tableau Dashboard (Desktop or Cloud/Server) **When** the extension is loaded **Then** the extension shell renders correctly in both environments (FR29) ## Tasks / Subtasks - [x] **Task 1: Add Tableau Extensions API runtime script to `index.html`** (AC: 1, 2, 4) - [x] Add script tag before closing `` in `autom9-extension/index.html`: ```html ``` - [x] This is the runtime that provides `window.tableau` — without it `initializeAsync` is undefined even with the types package installed - [x] **Task 2: Create `autom9.trex` manifest** (AC: 1, 4) - [ ] Create `autom9-extension/autom9.trex` with exact XML structure below (Tableau ignores non-XML content): ```xml en_US 1.4 http://localhost:5173 read autom9 AI planning assistant for consultants ``` - [x] `source-location` URL = the extension frontend URL (Vite dev server at localhost:5173). This is NOT the backend URL. The backend URL is configured separately via `VITE_BACKEND_URL`. - [x] `id` must be unique reverse-DNS format; `min-api-version` 1.4 supports Tableau Desktop 2019.4+ - [x] `permission` value `read` = read worksheet data; do NOT add write permissions - [x] **Task 3: Add `CORS_ORIGINS` to backend config and wire CORS middleware** (AC: 3) - [x] In `autom9-backend/app/core/config.py`, add one field to `Settings` class: ```python CORS_ORIGINS: str = "http://localhost:5173" ``` Use a default so existing tests are unaffected. Comma-separated list format: `"http://localhost:5173,https://prod.tableau.com"`. - [x] In `autom9-backend/app/main.py`, add CORS middleware **before** route definitions (order matters in ASGI middleware stack): ```python from fastapi.middleware.cors import CORSMiddleware app.add_middleware( CORSMiddleware, allow_origins=[o.strip() for o in settings.CORS_ORIGINS.split(",")], allow_credentials=True, allow_methods=["*"], allow_headers=["*"], ) ``` - [x] Update `autom9-backend/.env.example`: add `CORS_ORIGINS=http://localhost:5173` - [x] Update root `docker-compose.yml` `app` service `environment:` block: add `CORS_ORIGINS: ${CORS_ORIGINS:-http://localhost:5173}` - [x] **Task 4: Create `src/lib/tableau.ts` — Tableau API wrapper** (AC: 2) - [x] Create `autom9-extension/src/lib/tableau.ts`: ```typescript /** * Thin wrapper around window.tableau.extensions.initializeAsync(). * Resolves immediately when Tableau runtime is absent (dev/test environment). */ export async function initializeExtension(): Promise { if (typeof window === 'undefined' || !('tableau' in window)) { // No Tableau runtime — running in dev/test outside Tableau Desktop/Cloud return; } await (window as typeof window & { tableau: { extensions: { initializeAsync: () => Promise } } }) .tableau.extensions.initializeAsync(); } ``` - [x] Do NOT use `import tableau from '@tableau/extensions-api-types'` — the types package provides ambient type declarations only; the runtime is the CDN script.
